newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices end mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices end mixed.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended mixed Wednesday with the spotlight on new issues as the market headed into Thursday's August Producer Price Index report.
"A few things are up, a few things are down," said one trader, who gauged muni prices as unchanged to mixed.
A municipal analyst also said levels were difficult to call, but judged prices unchanged to 1/8 point lower overall.
"It is kind of a mixed bag, no real definition," he said.

The analyst said high-grade issues were unchanged overall, but showed slight weakness in the intermediate range and slight improvement on the longer end. Dollar bonds ended unchanged to down 1/8, he said.
Thursday's PPI number should provide some price direction, the trader said.
"I think that the number will get us to move with more conviction," he said.
Economist polled by Reuters expect August producer prices to rise 0.1 percent both overall and in the core rate, which excludes the more volatile food and energy prices.
New issue pricing was firm, the analyst said.
"Some people have been describing it as agressive or strong," he said. "I don't think it's aggressive, I think it's right in line."

A $184 million Broward County, Fla., offering topped the negotiated list. PaineWebber Inc repriced the professional sports facilities revenue bond issue, cutting yields in several maturities, and lowering the top tax-exempt yield in 2028 to 5.92 percent from 5.95 percent.

On the competitive side, Morgan Stanley & Co won $115 million Wisconsin general obligation bonds at a true interest cost of 5.559 percent. JP Morgan Securities Inc won $111 million Mississippi GOs at a true interest cost of 5.4738 percent.
JP Morgan also won $62 million Dallas, Texas, water and sewer bonds at a 5.51 percent net interest cost. Merrill Lynch & Co won $62 million Florida Housing Finance Agency bonds at a 6.07 percent TIC.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract was up 2/32 at 111-23/32. The December T-bond contract was up 4/32 at 106-25/32. The MOB spread was 158 ticks.
The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed unchanged at 95-17/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
